# Replica Set Transactions — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Replica Set Transactions. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-20 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB Jira issue SERVER-88746 documents a snapshot-isolation violation in replica-set transactions on version 7.0.0 when writes raced with a collection drop or rename; the issue lists 7.0.10 as the fix version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-05-06) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-88746
- [statement] With transaction commit write concern w:1, MongoDB acknowledges after the primary applies the commit, so a failover can roll the transaction back before replication; when the former primary rejoins, it reverts writes that were not replicated to secondaries. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-rollbacks.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-rollback-in-replicaset/
- [statement] Transaction-level read concern snapshot or majority guarantees majority-committed reads only when commit uses write concern majority; without majority at commit, those read concerns alone do not provide that guarantee. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB keeps a replica-set transaction's changes invisible to outside operations until commit; on commit, all changes become visible together rather than as a partial subset. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-rollbacks.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB’s production manual says standalone deployments do not support transactions and that replica sets support multi-document transactions. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration/
- [statement] The current production manual requires every replica-set member to have featureCompatibilityVersion 4.0 or later for transactions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration/
- [statement] A transaction containing reads must use read preference primary, and all operations in that transaction route to the same replica-set member. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/why-can-t-read-preference-be-secondary-in-a-transaction/204432
- [statement] Within a transaction, readConcern snapshot guarantees a snapshot of majority-committed data only if commitTransaction uses writeConcern majority; without majority at commit, that guarantee does not hold. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md
- [statement] A transaction committed with writeConcern w:1 can be rolled back after failover; writeConcern majority acknowledges after the commit is applied to a majority of voting members. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.percona.com/sites/default/files/presentations/Running-MongoDB-Production-Webinar-Pt-III.pdf
- [statement] A 2022 formal-verification paper models the REPLICASET transaction protocol separately and reports that it satisfies a Strong-SI variant of snapshot isolation under the paper’s formal model. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14946
- [statement] Jepsen’s MongoDB 4.2.6 evaluation found snapshot-isolation anomalies, but it tested a two-shard cluster whose config replica set and data shards each had three members, so it does not isolate replica-set-only transactions. (high confidence) — https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6 · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://github.com/jepsen-io/mongodb
- [statement] MongoDB's replication README says durability of a single replica-set transaction is not guaranteed until commitTransaction is majority committed; it also says unprepared transactions in progress are aborted during stepdown and are not recovered on failover. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-rollbacks.md
- [statement] A 2022 formal-verification paper models MongoDB's replica-set transaction protocol from documentation and source code and reports that its REPLICASET model satisfies Realtime-SI. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14946 · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/repl/README.md
- [statement] MongoDB documents an exception to majority durability: if writeConcernMajorityJournalDefault is false, a transient loss of a majority of replica-set nodes can still allow majority-acknowledged writes to roll back. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-rollbacks.md · keywords: Replica Set Transactions · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md
